data.content_ref: inline:SRC_001 demands a causal mechanism but supplies only an empirical-inductive fit: 'we infer a linear pricing function P(n) = (2/7)·n' from one data point. For THIS problem, 21 is an exact integer multiple of 7 (21 = 3·7), so the cost follows by the bundle definition itself — three disjoint bundles of 7-for-$2 cost 3·$2 = $6 — with no induction over unseen multiples required. By framing the step as inductive generalization from a single datapoint and withholding the partition/bundle mechanism, the target fails to provide the causal route the problem supplies, leaving the $6 answer resting on an unnecessary skeptical conjecture rather than a deterministic grouping operation.
